what_broke: Carta company_embeddings.json was empty (0 semantic units) — BFS crawl returned nothing
root_cause: Two issues: (1) BFS queue never seeded with base_url when no seed_urls provided — only sitemap/RSS pages were added but sitemaps returned 403. (2) carta.com is behind Cloudflare JS challenge — all httpx requests return 403 regardless of User-Agent.
fix_applied: (1) Always append base_url to priority_queue. (2) Added 3-tier fallback: httpx → Playwright headless Chromium → Wayback Machine. Site-level flag skips httpx after first CF detection.
lesson: Always seed BFS with base_url regardless of seed_urls. Major sites use Cloudflare — need headless browser fallback for reliable crawling.
recurrence_prevention: base_url is now always in priority_queue. Playwright fallback handles CF-protected sites automatically.

what_broke: Langfuse tracing errors: 'Langfuse' object has no attribute 'trace' — all tracing silently failed during live pipeline run
root_cause: tracing.py was written for Langfuse v2 API (lf.trace(), target.generation(), target.span()) but langfuse 3.14.1 was installed. v3 removed these methods entirely.
fix_applied: Rewrote tracing.py to use v3 SDK API: lf.trace() → lf.start_span() + span.update_trace(session_id=...), target.generation() → target.start_generation() + gen.end(), target.span() → target.start_span(), usage= → usage_details=, span.end(**kwargs) → span.update(**kwargs) then span.end().
lesson: Always verify SDK API against installed version, not docs that may describe a different version. Langfuse v3 is a breaking change from v2. Also note: start_generation is already deprecated in 3.14.1 in favor of start_observation(as_type='generation').
recurrence_prevention: v3 API is now used throughout. Monitor for start_observation migration when upgrading langfuse.

what_broke: Trafilatura flattens structural HTML elements — ordered_list_count, definition_list_count, table_count all zero
root_cause:
trafilatura.extract() converts
    ,
    ,

    tags in its HTML output. Counting elements on trafilatura output yields 0 for these structural elements.
fix_applied: Implemented dual-soup architecture: _extract_main_content() for text (trafilatura), _extract_structural_html() for element counting (semantic-tag-only, no trafilatura). Each path scoped separately.

what_broke: textstat.flesch_kincaid_grade() failed with NLTK LookupError — cmudict not found
root_cause: textstat internally uses NLTK cmudict for syllable counting. The cmudict corpus was not downloaded, and SSL certificate verification failed when attempting to download.
fix_applied: Downloaded cmudict manually with ssl._create_unverified_context workaround. The S4 code wraps textstat calls in try/except with default 0.0 on failure.
lesson: textstat depends on NLTK corpora. Ensure cmudict is available in deployment environments. The try/except guard handles graceful degradation.
recurrence_prevention: try/except guard around reading_level computation. Non-English text also skips reading level (defaults to 0.0).

what_broke: Persona and style guide agents produce .draft.md files that are never promoted to .md — _write_and_mirror() never executes
root_cause: Three-part failure chain: (1) CLI scripts called graph.invoke() but never checked result['__interrupt__'] — they printed empty results and exited. (2) core/research/graphs/pipeline.py caught GraphInterrupt exception which is dead code in LangGraph >=1.0 (invoke returns normally with __interrupt__ in dict instead of raising). (3) The API runner was the ONLY path that correctly handled interrupts, but CLI users had no working path.
fix_applied: (1) Created scripts/_cli_approval.py shared helper with MemorySaver checkpointer + interactive terminal approval loop. (2) Updated all 4 CLI scripts to use it. (3) Replaced dead GraphInterrupt catch in pipeline.py with __interrupt__ dict check. (4) Added _cleanup_drafts node on reject path in all 3 research graphs to delete orphaned .draft.md files.
lesson: LangGraph >=1.0 completely changed the interrupt model — interrupt() no longer raises GraphInterrupt, it returns __interrupt__ in the result dict. Any code catching GraphInterrupt is silently dead. Always verify LangGraph API behavior against the installed version.
recurrence_prevention: All graph invocations now check result.get('__interrupt__') instead of catching exceptions. Shared _cli_approval.py helper ensures consistent interrupt handling across CLI scripts.

what_broke: Content engine HITL disconnected from API task runner — auto_approve was hardcoded to False in pipeline.py line 384, and run_content_pipeline_task() didn't pass task_store/event_bus for Stage 4 HITL
root_cause: Two issues: (1) content pipeline Stage 4 passed auto_approve=input_data.auto_approve to run_content_review() correctly after fix, but before the fix it was hardcoded False. (2) run_content_pipeline_task() called run_content_generation() without passing task_store/event_bus, so the content review graph had no way to pause for API-driven HITL approval.
fix_applied: (1) Fixed auto_approve passthrough. (2) Added task_id/task_store/event_bus optional params to run_content_generation(). (3) Added _run_content_review_hitl() function that builds per-brief content review graphs with MemorySaver and uses task_store.wait_for_approval() for interrupt/resume. (4) run_content_pipeline_task() now passes all three params through.
lesson: When adding HITL to a new pipeline, ensure the task runner passes task_store and event_bus all the way down to the graph layer. The graph needs the checkpointer, and the runner needs the approval queue.
recurrence_prevention: Content pipeline now has explicit task_store/event_bus params. API path uses _run_content_review_hitl() with full HITL support.

what_broke: math domain error in _pearson() — math.sqrt received negative value from floating-point imprecision
root_cause: Pearson correlation formula computes `product = (n * sx2 - sx * sx) * (n * sy2 - sy * sy)`. When data values are nearly identical, floating-point cancellation can make the product slightly negative (e.g., -1e-15), causing math.sqrt() to throw ValueError.
fix_applied: Added guard: `if product <= 0: return 0.0` before `denom = math.sqrt(product)` in _pearson() function.
lesson: Any math.sqrt() call on a computed product should guard against negative values from floating-point imprecision. This is a common issue with variance/covariance calculations.
recurrence_prevention: Guard clause before sqrt. Test with `pytest.approx()` for floating-point comparisons instead of exact equality.

what_broke: 25 existing registration tests failed after adding password min_length=8 constraint (C3 fix)
root_cause: Existing test_registration.py used short passwords like 'p1', 'pass1', 'pass' in API-level tests. After adding Field(min_length=8) to LoginRequest and RegisterRequest, Pydantic validation rejected these with 422.
fix_applied: Updated all API-level test passwords to meet the 8-character minimum: 'p1'→'password01', 'pass1'→'securepass1', 'pass'→'securepass'. Only changed API-level tests (unit tests for AuthStore.register_user() keep short passwords since the constraint is on the API model, not the store).
lesson: When adding validation constraints to request models, always check existing test fixtures that use those models. API-level tests hit the validation layer; store-level tests bypass it.
recurrence_prevention: Run full test suite after any validation change. Keep unit tests (store-level) and integration tests (API-level) aware of which layer enforces the constraint.
